sections.label: Legal aid Bill changes
sections.summary: The Bill sets means criteria in subsidiary legislation, allows flexible aid, and improves legal aid administration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill does three things: first, it provides for the means criteria to be set out in subsidiary legislation; second, it provides for greater flexibility for aid to be given to those who might fail the means criteria; and third, it improves the administration of legal aid.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A significant clause of the Bill is clause 7(a), which provides for means criteria to be set out in subsidiary legislation instead of the Act.

sections.label: Revised means criteria indicators
sections.summary: Revised means criteria will align with social support schemes, using per capita household income and residence annual value.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The revised means criteria will be aligned with those more commonly used by current social support schemes, and reference indicators, such as (a) the per capita household income (PCHI), and (b) the annual value (AV) of the applicant’s place of residence, and his savings and investments.

sections.label: New means criteria implementation
sections.summary: Applicants need no documentary proof of deductibles, and qualifying limits will be set in subsidiary legislation next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Applicants will no longer need to provide various documentary proof of deductibles and, in setting the new PCHI limits, we intend to incorporate most of the permitted deductibles within the current means criteria to minimise the risk that applicants could be disadvantaged by the switch over from disposable income to gross income.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We will set out the qualifying limits for the new means criteria in subsidiary legislation next year, to account for the 2018, or the latest, income data.

sections.label: Ministerial Grant of Aid direction
sections.summary: Clause 7(b) lets the Minister direct a Grant of Aid to applicants failing means criteria if just and proper.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 7(b) allows the Minister to direct the Director to issue a Grant of Aid to an applicant who does not satisfy the means criteria, if the Minister is of the opinion that it is just and proper that legal aid be granted to this applicant.

sections.label: Specialist Legal Executives duties
sections.summary: Specially-trained Legal Executives will provide legal advice and may appear in Court for certain matters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Some of the appointed public officers will be specially-trained Legal Executives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: These "Specialist Legal Executives" will be authorised to provide legal advice to applicants and may also appear in Court for certain matters, such as uncontested divorces.

sections.label: Free additional Court documents
sections.summary: Clause 10 amends the Act to let aided persons obtain additional Court documents free of charge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 10 amends the Act to allow aided persons to obtain additional Court documents free of charge.

sections.label: Director's power for legal advice contributions
sections.summary: Clause 17 re-enacts section 9 as new section 22A, clarifying the Director may require contributions for legal advice cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 17 re-enacts the existing section 9 as a new section 22A, to clarify that the Director has the power to require contributions for legal advice cases.

sections.label: Removing current means test
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 21 remove the current means test in the Second Schedule, aligning it with other agencies and welfare services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Coming back to the Bill, clauses 7 and 21 remove the current means test in the Second Schedule of the current Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Currently, the merit test comprises the disposable income test and disposable capital test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The amendment allows the means test to be brought in line with what is currently used among other agencies and welfare services.

sections.label: Expanded scope of legal assistance
sections.summary: Clause 10 expands legal assistance so other relevant Court documents, besides judge's notes of evidence, may be provided without fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The scope of legal assistance is expanded under clause 10 where other relevant Court documents, besides judge’s notes of evidence, may be provided without fees.

sections.label: Means test criteria since 1958
sections.summary: The means test criteria have been in place since 1958, yet around 90% of applications passed the preliminary means test over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The current means test criteria, which take into account the applicant’s disposable income and disposable capital, have been in place since 1958.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Even with such stringent means test criteria, there has consistently been a high percentage of applications, at around 90%, which passed the preliminary means test for legal aid over the past five years.

sections.label: Legal aid application case types
sections.summary: Over five years, about 50% of applicants sought legal aid for matrimonial cases, 10% for monetary claims and 7% for probate matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, about 50% of applicants sought legal aid for matrimonial cases, 10% for monetary claims and 7% for probate matters.

sections.label: Public Trustee and HDB flat estates
sections.summary: The Public Trustee administers estates not exceeding $50,000 but cannot administer an estate where the deceased was sole lessee of an HDB flat and a child may inherit it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: While the Public Trustee administers estates of deceased persons where the value of the estate does not exceed $50,000, the Public Trustee is unable to administer the estate where the deceased was the sole lessee of an HDB flat and a child is eligible to inherit the whole or part of the flat.

sections.label: PCHI and AV adoption
sections.summary: Adopting PCHI and AV of residence, savings and investments replaces the disposable income and disposable capital arrangement, and is simpler and clearer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The adoption of PCHI and the AV of the applicant's place of residence, savings and investments to replace the current arrangement, which is based on disposable income and disposable capital, is simpler and clearer.

sections.label: LAB progress since 1958
sections.summary: LAB has received about 400,000 legal aid applications to date, and about 9,000 applications in 2017 alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is commendable to witness the progress of LAB since 1958.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that, to date, it has received about 400,000 applications for legal aid and, in 2017 alone, it received about 9,000 applications.

sections.label: DOT women beneficiaries
sections.summary: Since 2014, DOT has enabled 150 women to find jobs and start business projects, with some 40% being single mothers with secondary education or below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since its inception in 2014, DOT has enabled 150 women to find jobs and start business projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some 40% of these beneficiaries are single mothers with low education – secondary school and below.

sections.label: Director General aid discretion
sections.summary: The Ministry accepted suggestions allowing the Director General discretion to grant aid if just and proper, and a new LAB system from next year will speed access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened to see that the Ministry has taken on board our suggestions in allowing the Director general discretion to grant aid if it is just and proper to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It was announced just last week that, from next year, a new system set up by LAB will help applicants access legal aid more quickly by allowing lawyers to browse and select cases, and legal aid applicants to check the status of their applications.

sections.label: 2013 Act criteria relaxation
sections.summary: When the Act was amended in 2013, criteria were relaxed to raise qualifying citizens and PRs from 17% to 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When the Act was amended in 2013, the criteria was relaxed to increase the percentage of qualifying citizens and PRs from 17% to 25%.

sections.label: Tracking legal costs trends
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry tracks trends in legal costs and the proportion of households for whom legal representation remains inaccessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Is the Ministry tracking the trends in legal costs and the proportion of households for whom legal representation remains inaccessible?

sections.label: Expedited legal aid appeal process
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether an expedited process could assess extending legal aid to an aided person wishing to appeal, given strict appeal timelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Again, considering the strict timelines that must be adhered to in an appeal, would the Minister consider an expedited process for assessing whether to extend legal aid to an aided person who wishes to file an appeal?

sections.label: Simplifying means test assessment
sections.summary: Focusing on per capita income, home AV, savings and investments instead of several components would expedite assessment, though some dependants are not counted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Instead of considering several components of disposable income and capital, focusing on the main categories of the applicant's per capita income, home AV, savings and investments will help to expedite the assessment process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, an applicant may need to support parents, siblings or other vulnerable family members who do not stay with him under the same roof and thus are not considered during the computation of per capita income.

sections.label: Negative net worth definition
sections.summary: An applicant has negative net worth when his personal liabilities exceed his personal assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, if an applicant has a negative net worth, that means his personal liabilities exceed his personal assets.

sections.label: Deferment payment scheme legal fees
sections.summary: A deferment payment scheme for legal fees may be useful for those who are cash-strapped or asset-rich but cash-poor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, a deferment payment scheme for legal fees may be useful for those who are cash-strapped or who are asset-rich but cash-poor.

sections.label: Means test eligibility reform
sections.summary: A key reform in the Bill is changes to the means test used to assess eligibility for legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A key reform in the Bill is the changes to the means test to be used to assess eligibility for legal aid.

sections.label: PCHI means test and flexibility
sections.summary: The approach may be unfair to the family, but the Bill's PCHI means test and LAB flexibility will address this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In my respectful view, such an approach may operate unfairly against the family as it did not adequately take into account the circumstances surrounding the mentally incapacitated son and the reason for the application in Court in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am glad to note, however, that if this Bill is passed, then this issue will be taken care of because the PCHI will be adopted as the means test, both the income of the father and his son will be taken into account to assess the father's means more holistically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: LAB will also be vested with powers to exercise greater flexibility to provide targeted help to applicants in extenuating circumstances.

sections.label: Minister's discretion to grant aid
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Minister direct the Director of Legal Aid to issue a Grant of Aid even if the applicant fails the means criteria, if just and proper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Apart from the new means test, the Bill now provides that the Minister may direct the Director of Legal Aid to issue a Grant of Aid even though the Director is of the opinion that the applicant does not satisfy the prescribed means criteria, if the Minister is of the opinion that it is just and proper for legal aid to be granted.

sections.label: Clarification on legal aid resources
sections.summary: A Member seeks clarification on whether additional resources are needed for the Legal Aid Bureau given the shift to household-based criteria, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would be grateful for a clarification on the statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note that the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) has stated that the qualifying limit for the PCHI test will be set such that there will be no material impact on the number of households who are eligible for legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, there would presumably be some increase in eligible cases given the shift from individual-based criteria to household-based criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would there not be a need for additional resources to be provided to LAB to deal with this?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Act has been reviewed regularly over the years to ensure this goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I support the amendment Bill for its progressive changes made in the way that we assess means eligibility for legal aid to ensure that justice remains accessible by all.

sections.label: New updated means criteria
sections.summary: The Bill proposes new means criteria that have been updated and will simplify the application for legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the Bill currently before us, there are proposals to establish new means criteria that have been updated and will simplify the application for legal aid.

sections.label: Discretion for applicants not meeting criteria
sections.summary: The Legal Aid Bureau is constrained by the Act to assist only those fulfilling prescribed criteria, and amendments are proposed to allow discretion for others needing help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the moment, LAB is constrained by the Act in its present form and can only provide assistance to those who can fulfil the prescribed criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, grateful that amendments have been proposed to allow discretion in granting legal aid to those who may not completely fulfil the prescribed criteria, but nonetheless still require help.

sections.label: Means criteria in subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: The Bill proposes giving the Ministry flexibility to set new means criteria in subsidiary legislation, aligned to criteria used in social support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This requirement also often delays the process because the applicant would need to set aside time to look for and prepare the documents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, very pleased to note that the Bill proposes to give the Ministry the flexibility to establish new means criteria to be set out in the subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note the Ministry’s efforts in reviewing the means criteria, to update and simplify the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I also note that the plan is to align the means criteria to those commonly used in current social support schemes.

sections.label: Minister's discretion for just cases
sections.summary: The Member is grateful for provisions in the Bill giving the Minister discretion to grant legal aid if it is deemed just and proper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, we should endeavour to help as many as possible and we need to look at some measures to be able to address this gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, grateful that there are provisions in this Bill to give the Minister discretion to grant legal aid if it is deemed just and proper.

sections.label: Family law assistance scheme proposal
sections.summary: The Chief Justice proposed a low bono family law assistance scheme for the sandwich class, which is being looked into, with possible CPD points for pro bono and low bono work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the Opening of the Legal Year this year, Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon, proposed a family law assistance scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The idea is to develop a low bono model to increase access to legal services for those in the sandwich class who are embroiled in family disputes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is a meaningful suggestion which is being looked into.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There may also be a further need to incentivise lawyers with Continuing Professional Development (CPD) points to recognise them for efforts in pro bono as well as low bono work.

sections.label: Director appointing unqualified public officers
sections.summary: Clause 3A empowers the Director of Legal Aid to appoint suitable and experienced public officers who are not qualified persons under the Legal Professional Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, clause 3A states empowering the Director of Legal Aid to appoint "suitable and experienced" public officers who are not qualified persons under the Legal Professional Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And will it compromise the interest of the aided person in representing his case?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that legal aid is provided to both Singaporeans and PRs.

sections.label: Director exercising power instead of board
sections.summary: Clause 7(a) allows the Director to exercise this new power instead of a board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, clause 7(a) allows the Director to exercise this new power instead of a board.

sections.label: Legal aid cost in discretionary framework
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the cost of legal aid provided will be considered in the discretionary framework, noting serious lawsuits can cost tens of thousands of dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is another thing to ask the sandwich class to take on a very serious lawsuit which can go on to tens of thousands of dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, will the cost of the legal aid that is being provided be considered in the discretionary framework?

sections.label: LAB applications and means test
sections.summary: In the past 10 years, LAB received about 97,100 applications, of which 88,800, or more than 90%, passed the preliminary means test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the past 10 years, LAB had received a total of 97,100 applications approximately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Of these, 88,800, or more than 90%, passed the preliminary means test.

sections.label: New criteria replacing disposable income and capital
sections.summary: MinLaw will adopt the PCHI and AV of the applicant's place of residence, savings and investments as new criteria to replace disposable income and disposable capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MinLaw will adopt the PCHI and AV of the applicant’s place of residence, savings and investments as the new criteria to replace the current disposable income and disposable capital criteria.

sections.label: Qualifying limit for means criteria
sections.summary: The qualifying limit will be set later in subsidiary legislation using 2018 income data, keeping roughly 25% of households eligible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The qualifying limit for the new means criteria will be set later in subsidiary legislation, as I said earlier, to take into account the 2018 income data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But it will be set at a level where there will be no material impact on the number of households which will remain eligible for legal aid, and it will be set at a level which would ensure that a similar level of households at present, which is approximately 25%, will be maintained.

sections.label: Retaining coverage and assessing liabilities
sections.summary: Coverage is retained at present levels covering about 25% of households, and liabilities such as debts are not generally excluded in means assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the most recent review leading up to this Bill, we had taken into account these factors in deciding to retain the coverage at the present levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And as I mentioned earlier, at this level, approximately 25% of households are covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Murali Pillai also asked, on a related note, if we would consider circumstances where families are put into significant expense as a result of intervening events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We do not generally exclude liabilities, such as debts, when we assess an applicant's means.

sections.label: Applicant who paid off debts
sections.summary: A person who liquidated savings and investments to pay debts may be considered for assistance if still within the means criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: He would not be considered, in that situation, a person of limited means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, if that person or the applicant has liquidated his savings and investments to pay off the debts and thereafter, remains in a financial situation as would allow him to come within the means criteria, then yes, that person will be considered for assistance.

sections.label: Bill provides flexibility and discretion
sections.summary: The Bill does not expand coverage or consider negative net worth and non-household family members, but provides greater flexibility and discretion for deserving applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At the same time, whilst we are not expanding the coverage or considering the negative net worth and family members living in a different household when assessing means, the Bill, as I said earlier, does provide for greater flexibility and discretion for aid to be granted to deserving applicants.

sections.label: Appointing Legal Executives
sections.summary: Best Legal Executives may be appointed by the Director to provide legal advice and represent applicants in Court and at mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We feel that many of them are capable of doing more and can be made to do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we will allow our best Legal Executives to be appointed by the Director to provide legal advice and also represent applicants in Court proceedings and at mediation.

sections.label: Limiting officers to simple divorces
sections.summary: Such officers will initially be limited to simpler uncontested divorce proceedings where matrimonial assets are $1 million or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Even then, for a start, we intend to limit the cases where such officers will take up to simpler uncontested divorce proceedings where the matrimonial assets are $1 million or less, as a starting point.

sections.label: Director granting aid directly
sections.summary: Allowing the Director to grant aid in straightforward cases can speed up the applicant's case by up to two weeks without waiting for the Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Allowing the Director in such cases to grant aid for straightforward matters will help, and not hinder, the applicant’s case by up to two weeks, as the Director can now immediately determine whether in that case aid should be granted or not, assuming the means criteria is satisfied, without waiting for the Board to convene.

sections.label: PRs pay higher contribution
sections.summary: The criteria remain the same, but permanent residents granted legal aid will generally pay a higher contribution towards their case costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The criteria will be the same, but PRs will generally be charged a higher contribution towards the costs incurred for their case, if they are granted legal aid.

sections.label: Fresh merits evaluation and urgent aid
sections.summary: Changed circumstances may affect appeal merits, so fresh evaluation is useful; urgent applicants may receive provisional aid if likely to pass means and merits tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Circumstances in such a case, however, which may affect the merits of bringing or resisting an appeal, or in enforcing a judgment, may have changed, and it would be useful to have regard to this in the fresh merits evaluation to ensure that the grant of aid still remains appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I would also like to assure the Member that where an applicant requires aid as a matter of urgency, for example, when an appeal is due to be filed, the Director may issue a Grant of Aid on a provisional basis, if the Director is of the view that the applicant is likely to satisfy the means test and is likely to have a reasonable ground for appealing against the decision.

sections.label: Funding for CLAS criminal defence
sections.summary: Since 2015 the Government gave close to $6 million to the Law Society's Pro Bono Services Office running CLAS, which assigns lawyers to accused persons who cannot afford one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Since 2015, the Government has provided close to $6 million of funding support to the Law Society's Pro Bono Services Office which runs CLAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: CLAS, in turn, assigns lawyers to accused persons who have been charged with a crime and who cannot afford hiring a lawyer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in this way, this has resulted in expanded assistance to criminal defence cases, as CLAS has been able to assist almost four times as many applicants in 2017, compared to pre-2015 before the funding was made available.

sections.label: LAB referral protocols for victims
sections.summary: Since 2016 LAB established referral protocols for family violence victims with PAVE and with MSF for social service needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Since 2016, LAB has also established referral protocols for family violence victims with the Centre for Promoting Alternatives to Violence (PAVE), and with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) for those with social service needs, such as housing problems, family dysfunction and also addiction issues.

sections.label: Full Domestic Exclusion Order obtained
sections.summary: LAB eventually successfully obtained the full Domestic Exclusion Order for the applicant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: LAB eventually successfully obtained the full Domestic Exclusion Order for the applicant.

sections.label: Legal aid means criteria
sections.summary: LAB's work is simplified by simplifying means criteria, allowing flexibility for aid, and improving legal aid administration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As Members know, it is in its 60th year this year LAB's work is simplified by, first, simplifying the means criteria, which makes the process quicker, easier and also fairer; second, providing for more flexibility for aid to be given to those who might fail the means criteria, but nonetheless still cannot afford legal services for a number of reasons; and finally, improving the overall the administration of legal aid.

sections.label: Mediation and Small Claims Tribunal
sections.summary: Mediation infrastructure exists and the Small Claims Tribunal claims limit was raised from $10,000 to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we have built up the infrastructure for mediation to take place; community mediation has been happening for a while.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And we have also raised the claims limit recently for the Small Claims Tribunal from $10,000 to $20,000, so as to allow more to benefit from this quick and relatively inexpensive forum.
